grammarOverrides.from: French aimer uses the person who likes as its subject: j’aime, tu aimes, il/elle aime, nous aimons, vous aimez, ils/elles aiment. Unlike Spanish gustar, the number of liked things does not control the verb. Use aimer + definite article for a general interest (j’aime la musique) and aimer + infinitive for an activity (nous aimons étudier). Negation surrounds the conjugated verb: Luis n’aime pas le café.
grammarOverrides.to: French aimer uses the person who likes as its subject: j’aime, tu aimes, il/elle aime, nous aimons, vous aimez, ils/elles aiment. The subject determines the form of aimer. Use aimer + definite article for a general interest (j’aime la musique) and aimer + infinitive for an activity (nous aimons étudier). Negation surrounds the conjugated verb: Luis n’aime pas le café.

grammarOverrides.from: French vouloir is irregular: je veux, tu veux, il/elle veut, nous voulons, vous voulez, ils/elles veulent. Place an infinitive after it to express an intended action: Je veux visiter ma famille. Nous voulons manger ensemble. French does not follow the Spanish e-to-ie stem-change rule; learn the French forms as a separate pattern. Je voudrais is a softer, more polite request, but this lesson practices the present tense.
grammarOverrides.to: French vouloir is irregular: je veux, tu veux, il/elle veut, nous voulons, vous voulez, ils/elles veulent. Je voudrais is a softer, more polite request, but this lesson practices the present tense.

cautionOverrides.from: J’aime les livres remains j’aime even though livres is plural. Avoid copying Spanish me gusta / me gustan agreement into French.
cautionOverrides.to: J’aime les livres remains j’aime even though livres is plural. The subject determines verb agreement.
